tagline: From a mill town on Mount Shasta's slope toward Tule Lake.
intro: Out of McCloud on Mount Shasta’s southern slope, the Modoc Volcanic Scenic Byway takes Highway 89 and the road northeast toward Medicine Lake. McCloud was a lumber town in a very practical sense: its mill supplied electricity and steam heat to the houses as well as work.

Beyond Medicine Lake the route passes Lava Beds National Monument, where the Army kept its Modoc War command post, on the way to Tulelake, named for nearby Tule Lake. Snow closes the road around November.

moments.title: McCloud
moments.text: McCloud's company houses passed to private owners in 1965, and the mill that once heated and lit them last closed in 2002.

moments.title: Guillem’s Graveyard
moments.text: A marker in Lava Beds National Monument recalls the Army cemetery from the Modoc War, whose burials were later moved elsewhere.

moments.title: Tulelake
moments.text: Tulelake began with a public auction of town land in 1931, when more than a hundred lots sold.

practical: Snow usually closes the route around November, depending on snowfall; winter snow depths permit travel only by snowmobile or snow cat.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Modoc Volcanic National Scenic Byway
